title: Acids, Bases, and Salts: The pH Story

questions.question: A Brønsted–Lowry base is defined as a:
questions.rationale: Brønsted–Lowry (1923) bases accept protons; Arrhenius bases produce OH⁻ in water, and Lewis bases donate electron pairs.

questions.question: Which species is a Lewis acid that contains no hydrogen at all?
questions.rationale: BF₃ accepts an electron pair into boron's empty orbital — the Lewis definition covers acids with no H.

questions.question: Pure water at 25 °C has a pH of:
questions.rationale: On the 0–14 scale at 25 °C, pH 7 is neutral — H⁺ and OH⁻ concentrations are equal.

questions.question: Phenolphthalein turns what colour in a basic solution?
questions.rationale: Colourless below pH 8.3 and pink above it — the classic titration endpoint colour.

questions.question: Which salt dissolves to give an acidic solution?
questions.rationale: NH₄Cl comes from a strong acid plus weak base; the NH₄⁺ ion releases H⁺. Na₂CO₃ and CH₃COONa give basic solutions, NaCl neutral.

questions.question: Aqua regia — the mixture that dissolves gold — is:
questions.rationale: Three volumes of concentrated HCl to one of concentrated HNO₃ — 'royal water'.

questions.question: Tooth decay speeds up when mouth pH drops below about:
questions.rationale: Below pH 5.5, bacterial acids begin dissolving the calcium salts of tooth enamel.

questions.question: Plaster of Paris is chemically:
questions.rationale: Heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) removes most of the water, giving CaSO₄·½H₂O, which re-sets to gypsum when water is added.

questions.question: Which of these is a weak acid?
questions.rationale: Acetic acid ionizes only partially; HCl, HNO₃, and H₂SO₄ are strong, fully ionizing acids.

questions.question: The conjugate base of HCl is:
questions.rationale: Removing one proton from an acid gives its conjugate base: HCl → Cl⁻.
